what: The score combines normalized insertion distance, a modest depot-radial savings reward, and a capacity-aware one-step continuation statistic. The continuation term searches the remaining customers for a feasible successor that is both geographically close and leaves little residual capacity; if none fits, it penalizes the capacity that would be stranded when the route closes. Its influence increases as the route fills. Runtime is O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) per invocation with O(1) extra space.
why: Farthest-first route opening already creates a remote seed, so radial savings and insertion cost encourage coherent outward-to-inward clusters rather than consuming capacity on cheap central customers too early. The continuation term addresses the strong demand-packing pressure visible in small-capacity instances while still considering geometry, and cheapest insertion provides a sensible ordering for subsequent 2-opt. The rule is intentionally myopic: it considers only one possible successor, does not predict later routes or the exact effect of 2-opt, and its fixed weights may need validation across instance families.
